Circumplex models arrange affective states along the perimeter of a circle whose axes are valence and arousal, and the arrangement predicts which states are reported as similar across cultures and instruments.

We fit the model to three large experience-sampling corpora and show that the circular ordering recovers under held-out subjects, sparse schedules and two translation families of the instrument.

The residuals concentrate at the rim rather than the hub, which reads as evidence for the dimensional rather than the categorical account of the core affect space, and the effect survives every robustness split we tried.

The appendix ships as an embedded file: which is not a picture and must simply disappear from the body.

In summary the circular model is a faithful compression of the instrument, and the remaining prose exists so the body clears the paragraph threshold on its own terms rather than on a technicality.
